governing_table.code: Michigan Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Michigan amendments, Mich. Admin. Code R 408.30701 to R 408.30796)
governing_table.edition: 2021 (IPC 2021 second printing); Table 403.1 as rewritten by R 408.30758 (history: 2023 AACS)
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures
governing_table.quote: R 408.30758 Minimum number of fixtures. Rule 758. Sections 403.1, 403.1.1 and 403.3.1 and Table 403.1 of the code are amended to read as follows: 403.1. Minimum number of fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1.
governing_table.note: The Michigan Building Code deletes its own table: R 408.30401 adopts the 2021 IBC 'except for sections ... 2902 to 2902.6, Table 2902.1', and R 408.30419 amends 1210.1 to read 'The number and type of plumbing fixtures provided in an occupancy shall comply with the Michigan plumbing code.' (https://ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us/AdminCode/DownloadAdminCodeFile?FileName=R%20408.30401%20to%20R%20408.30499a.pdf)

fixtures.cities_may_amend_note: MCL 125.1508a(1): 'This act and the code apply throughout the state.' Cities enforce the state code; the statute read does not use the words 'may not amend', so the city agent should still check Detroit and Grand Rapids for local ordinances. https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-125-1508a

office.row_label: 2 Business, B: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial, and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: Table heading: 'WATER CLOSETS (URINALS SEE SECTION 419.2)'; no urinals required
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 [water closets, one entry across the male and female columns]; 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 [lavatories]

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly, A-2: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts
restaurant.urinals: Table heading: 'WATER CLOSETS (URINALS SEE SECTION 419.2)'; no urinals required
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 [male], 1 per 75 [female], 1 per 200 [lavatories]. Footnote d: 'The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.'

school.urinals: Table heading: 'WATER CLOSETS (URINALS SEE SECTION 419.2)'; no urinals required
school.quote: Educational facilities: 1 per 50 [water closets]; 1 per 50 [lavatories]; 1 per 100 [drinking fountains]; 1 service sink. Section 403.1 exception 4: 'Toilet facilities for childcare center, day care center, and nursery school facilities shall be provided in accordance with R 400.8101 to R 400.8840.'

sex_split.text: Total occupants are divided in half, unless approved statistics show another split. Michigan also lets the count be based on the actual number of occupants, backed by an affidavit from the owner.
sex_split.quote: 403.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: 1. The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50% of each sex. | 403.1 ... Exceptions: 1. The actual number of occupants determined by a supporting affidavit from the owner or agency.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole fixture, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, the fractional numbers for each occupancy shall be summed and rounded up to the next whole number. | Table footnote a: The fixtures shown are based on 1 fixture being the minimum required for the number of individuals indicated or any fraction of the number of individuals indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. They may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational occupancies and up to 50% in all others, in each toilet room. Each urinal needs partitions at both sides. Michigan's rewritten table heading points to 'Section 419.2' for urinals; in the 2021 IPC the substitution rule is section 424.2 (419.2 is about lavatories), so the cross-reference looks like a leftover from an earlier edition.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. | 405.3.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.
urinal_substitution.source_note: Read on UpCodes' copy of the 2021 IPC under Michigan (secondary). The LARA rules file contains no Michigan amendment to sections 424 or 405.3.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the building or tenant space holds 15 people or fewer in total (staff and customers), or in a shop holding 50 or fewer. Michigan's wording differs from the model code.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: R 408.30722 ... 403.2. Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for private facilities. 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 50 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 square feet gross per person. Restaurant dining room (assembly, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 square feet net. Classroom: 20 square feet net.
occupant_load.quote: Table 1004.5: Assembly without fixed seats, Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; Business areas 150 gross; Educational, Classroom area 20 net. | Michigan 403.1: 'The number of occupants shall be determined in accordance with the Michigan building code.'
occupant_load.source_note: Table 1004.5 read on UpCodes' copy of the 2021 Michigan Building Code (secondary). The LARA Part 4 rules file contains no amendment to section 1004.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. Business: 1 per 25 for the first 50 of each sex. 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's required toilets: 50% of 1 = 0.50, so 0 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

50 women, 50 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's required toilets: 50% of 2 = 1.00, so 1 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

100 women, 100 men. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1; total 3 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's required toilets: 50% of 3 = 1.50, so 1 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

200 women, 200 men. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3; total 5 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's required toilets: 50% of 5 = 2.50, so 2 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

25 women, 25 men. Restaurants: 1 per 75. 25/75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

50 women, 50 men. 50/75 = 0.67, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

100 women, 100 men. 100/75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

200 women, 200 men. 200/75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

25 women, 25 men. Educational: 1 per 50. 25/50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

50 women, 50 men. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

100 women, 100 men. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

200 women, 200 men. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets: 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2 (the code does not say how this fraction rounds; rounded down here so the limit is not exceeded).

fixtures.confidence_note: Table rows, split, rounding and the separate-facilities exception were read in the official LARA rules file. The urinal percentages and floor areas per person were read on UpCodes (secondary, medium).

hdpe_fire.section: 2021 Michigan Building Code, Section 803.9 (pointing to 803.1.1, NFPA 286)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Chapter 2 definition, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: 'The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; ...'
hdpe_fire.note: Read on UpCodes' copy of the 2021 Michigan Building Code (secondary). The official LARA Part 4 rules (R 408.30401 to R 408.30499a) adopt the 2021 IBC by reference and contain no amendment to Chapter 8, so the model text applies.

access.state_standard: Michigan barrier free design requirements: 1966 PA 1 (MCL 125.1351 to 125.1356), 2021 Michigan Building Code Chapter 11, and ICC A117.1 except sections 611 and 707. The rule gives no edition year; the 2021 Michigan Building Code's referenced-standards list (read on UpCodes) gives ICC A117.1-17 (2017).

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.5.1: the side wall needs a horizontal bar and a vertical bar. 604.5.1.2: 'A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.' Applies in wheelchair stalls (604.9.6) and on both sides of ambulatory stalls (604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical bar.
differences.quote: Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2.

differences.point: Toe clearance under the wheelchair stall's partitions
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.9.5.1: 12 inches high and 8 inches deep. Not required at the front where the stall is deeper than 64 inches (wall-hung toilet) or 67 inches (floor-mounted), or at the side where the stall is wider than 68 inches.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition'. Exception thresholds: 62 inches deep (wall-hung), 65 inches (floor-mounted), 66 inches wide.
differences.quote: The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members.

differences.state: 2021 Michigan Building Code 1110.2.4: 5 percent of the compartments wheelchair accessible; where toilets in stalls plus urinals total six or more, 5 percent ambulatory accessible in addition. The two only diverge from the federal count in very large toilet rooms (more than 20 stalls).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: 'at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition ... at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.'
differences.quote: Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.

differences.point: Where the wheelchair stall's door opening sits
differences.state: A117.1-2017 Table 604.9.3.1 gives two choices on each wall. Front partition: 56 inches minimum from the side wall nearest the toilet, or 4 inches maximum from the far side wall. Side partition: 52 inches minimum from the rear wall (wall-hung; 55 floor-mounted), or 4 inches maximum from the front partition.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.2: 'Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet. Where located in the side wall or partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the front partition.' A stall meeting the 4-inch federal placement meets both.
differences.quote: The farthest edge of the wheelchair accessible toilet compartment door opening shall be located in the front wall or partition or in the side wall or partition as required by Table 604.9.3.1.

differences.point: Family or assisted-use toilet room in large assembly and retail buildings
differences.state: 2021 Michigan Building Code 1110.2.1 requires one where six or more toilets (men's and women's together) are required.
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards have no requirement to provide a family or assisted-use toilet room (213.2 scopes the toilet rooms that are provided).
differences.quote: In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required.

access.same_as_federal: Stall sizes match: wheelchair stall 60 inches wide by 56 inches deep (wall-hung toilet) or 59 inches (floor-mounted); ambulatory stall 35 to 37 inches wide and 60 inches deep; doors self-closing with pulls on both sides (A117.1-2017 604.9.2.1, 604.10.2, 604.9.3; ADA 604.8.1.1, 604.8.2.1, 604.8.1.2).
access.process: No separate state registration or state accessibility plan review was found for private projects. Barrier free design is checked by the local or state building department with the building permit: MCL 125.1352(4), 'the approval of the appropriate local or state administrative authority shall be secured before the issuance of a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a facility used by the public'. Only the state Barrier Free Design Board can grant an exception (MCL 125.1355(8)); requests must reach the board at least 60 days before its meeting, with a fee (LARA board page). An alteration touching 50% or more of the floor area brings the whole building under the requirements (MCL 125.1352(2)(b)).
access.confidence_note: R 408.30427 and the statute were read on official pages. The A117.1 edition and its text, and Chapter 11 of the building code, were read on UpCodes.

single_user.rule: Single-user toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex. Michigan's rules do not amend this section, and Michigan's own 403.1.1 exception 3 refers to it.
single_user.quote: 403.1.2 Single-User Toilet and Bathing Room Fixtures. ... Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. | Michigan 403.1.1 exception 3: 'Distribution of the sexes is not required where single-user water closets and bathing room fixtures are provided in accordance with section 403.1.2.'

all_gender_shared.rule: Michigan's fixture-calculation rule provides for multiple-user rooms that serve all genders: fixtures are counted on the total occupant load, fixtures follow ICC A117.1, and every urinal must be in a stall. Each toilet used by the public or employees must be in its own compartment with a door (405.3.4). Open point: Michigan's rewritten section 403.2 on separate facilities lists three exceptions and none of them is the model code's all-gender exception, so confirm with the building department how it reads the two together.
all_gender_shared.quote: 403.1.1 ... Exceptions: ... 2. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixtures count shall be calculated at 100%, based on total occupant load. The minimum number of required plumbing fixtures shall be in accordance with table 403.1. In multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. | 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.

use_restrictions.rule: No enacted Michigan statute restricting who may use which restroom was found. House Bill 4024 of 2025 (student restrooms and changing areas in schools, by biological sex) passed the House on 2025-09-04 and was referred to the Senate Committee on Government Operations on 2025-09-09; the Legislature's bill page shows no later action.
use_restrictions.quote: Civil rights: privacy; restriction of student access to certain restrooms and changing areas based on biological sex; provide for. Creates new act. ... 9/09/2025 SJ 74 Pg. 906 REFERRED TO COMMITTEE ON GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS

other.rule: Michigan adds two rules to the building code: a building with baby changing stations in the women's restrooms must have them in the men's, and signs must show the route to public toilet rooms.
other.quote: 1210.5. Baby changing stations. A building or structure with baby changing stations in the women's restrooms shall have baby changing stations in the men's restrooms. 1210.6. Directional signage indicating the route to the public facilities.

public_wage.law: 2023 PA 10, MCL 408.1101 to 408.1126 (prevailing wages on state projects), effective February 13, 2024; amended by 2024 PA 110, effective April 2, 2025
public_wage.threshold_note: No dollar threshold appears in sections 1 to 4 as read. Coverage turns on the project: 'state project' means work on public buildings or schools that is authorized by a public contracting agent (a state officer, school board, state board or commission, or state institution supported in whole or in part by state funds) and 'sponsored or financed in whole or in part by this state'. A city building paid for only with city money is not within that wording; the city agent should check for a local ordinance.
public_wage.quote: MCL 408.1102(1): '... the rates of wages and fringe benefits to be paid to each class of mechanics by the bidder and all of its subcontractors must not be less than the wage and fringe benefit rates prevailing in the locality in which the work is to be performed.' MCL 408.1104: 'The commissioner shall establish prevailing wages and fringe benefits at the same rate that prevails on projects of a similar character in the locality under collective agreements or understandings between bona fide organizations of construction mechanics and their employers.' MCL 408.1101(a): '"Commissioner" means the department of labor and economic opportunity.' LEO page: 'All contractors and subcontractors must register and pay a $500 annual fee.'

sales_tax.local_taxes: None. Treasury: 'Michigan does not allow city or local units to impose sales tax.'

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable at 6%. A remote seller must collect once it had over $100,000 of gross sales or 200 or more transactions with Michigan customers in the previous calendar year. If the seller doesn't collect, the buyer owes 6% use tax.
shipped_goods.quote: A remote seller has nexus with Michigan and is required to report and pay sales or use tax if, in the previous calendar year, the remote seller made over $100,000 of gross sales or 200 or more separate transactions with Michigan customers. | Use tax of 6% must be paid to the State of Michigan on the total price of all taxable items brought into Michigan or purchases through the internet, by mail or by phone from out-of-state retailers that do not collect and remit sales or use tax from their customers.

sales_tax.freight_note: Not taxed since April 26, 2023 if the delivery charge is separately itemized on the invoice and the seller's books show it; otherwise it is part of the taxable price. Quote: 'Beginning April 26, 2023, most delivery and installation charges are not subject to sales and use taxes as long as the seller (i.e., the taxpayer): separately itemizes delivery and installation charges on an invoice to the customer. keeps books and records that show how the tax levied was calculated for these transactions.' Treasury treats 'handling, postage, freight, crating, and packing' as delivery charges. https://www.michigan.gov/taxes/business-taxes/sales-use-tax/delivery-and-installation-charges

install_labor.rule: A seller's installation charge is not taxed if it is separately itemized on the invoice and the seller's records support it; if not, it is taxed with the goods. A contractor improving real estate does not charge sales tax to its customer at all.
install_labor.quote: Installation charges are costs associated with the service of placing or setting up tangible items for use. ... Beginning April 26, 2023, most delivery and installation charges are not subject to sales and use taxes as long as the seller ... separately itemizes delivery and installation charges on an invoice to the customer [and] keeps books and records that show how the tax levied was calculated for these transactions. ... Because the delivery and installation charges were not separately stated, the delivery/installation fees are included in the sales price and are taxable.

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor is the consumer: it pays 6% sales or use tax on the materials it fixes to the building and may not charge tax to the customer, though it may include the tax in its price. If the customer buys the partitions from a retailer that collected Michigan tax, the installing contractor owes no use tax on them.
furnish_and_install.quote: A contractor is required to pay sales or use tax on all items used to provide the contractor's service, including equipment, supplies, materials (including materials affixed to and made a structural part of real estate located in Michigan) ... A contractor that pays sales or use tax on the property it uses and consumes in performing a construction contract ... may not charge sales or use tax directly to its customer. However, the contractor may include the amount of the tax in the total contract price as an overhead cost. | If the retailer (supplier) collects sales or use tax from its customer, the contractor is relieved of paying use tax for that property if the contractor can demonstrate that the sales tax was collected by the retailer (supplier.)

page.stalls_intro: Michigan counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional under Michigan's rules: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office, and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen on both sides.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A space that holds 15 people or fewer in total doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms, and Michigan lets an owner base the count on the actual number of occupants with a signed affidavit.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Michigan's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Michigan's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and Michigan's barrier free design rules set the sizes. The building department checks them with the permit, and only the state's Barrier Free Design Board can grant an exception.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Michigan extras:** the stall sizes match the federal ones, but Michigan's rules add an 18-inch vertical grab bar on the side wall of accessible stalls, and ask for more toe space under the wheelchair stall's partitions: 12 inches high and 8 inches deep, against 9 and 6 under the federal rules.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Michigan's rules provide for shared all-gender rooms: the toilet count is based on everyone in the building, every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door, and every urinal must be in a stall. Michigan's rule on separate men's and women's rooms doesn't list these rooms among its exceptions, so confirm the layout with your building department. No Michigan law in force sets who may use which restroom.
page.public_jobs: On schools and other public buildings paid for in whole or in part by the state, Michigan law requires at least the prevailing local wage and benefits, which the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity publishes by county, and contractors on those jobs must register with the state.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Michigan, an installation charge isn't taxed when it is listed separately on the invoice and the seller's records back it up. A contractor who supplies and installs partitions pays the 6% tax on the materials and can't add sales tax to your bill, though the tax may be built into the price.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxed at 6%. Freight isn't taxed when it is listed separately on the invoice. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state as use tax.
page.tax_rate_line: - **Sales tax:** 6% in {city}. Michigan has one statewide rate and no city or county sales tax.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Michigan Department of Treasury
sources: - Toilet counts in Michigan: [Michigan Plumbing Code rules, R 408.30701 to R 408.30796](https://ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us/AdminCode/DownloadAdminCodeFile?FileName=R%20408.30701%20to%20R%20408.30796.pdf) (LARA Bureau of Construction Codes), R 408.30758 (sections 403.1 and 403.1.1 and Table 403.1) and R 408.30722 (section 403.2, separate facilities). The Michigan Building Code leaves the count to the plumbing code: [Part 4 rules, R 408.30401 and R 408.30419](https://ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us/AdminCode/DownloadAdminCodeFile?FileName=R%20408.30401%20to%20R%20408.30499a.pdf). Urinal limits (2021 International Plumbing Code section 424.2), urinal partitions (405.3.5) and stall compartments (405.3.4) were read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/michigan/ipc-2021/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings). Checked 2026-11-24.
- Floor area per person: 2021 Michigan Building Code, Table 1004.5, read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/michigan/mi-building-code-2021/chapter/10/means-of-egress). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Fire test for solid plastic partitions: 2021 Michigan Building Code, Section 803.9 (NFPA 286 through Section 803.1.1), read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/michigan/mi-building-code-2021/chapter/8/interior-finishes); the [state's Part 4 rules](https://ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us/AdminCode/DownloadAdminCodeFile?FileName=R%20408.30401%20to%20R%20408.30499a.pdf) do not amend Chapter 8. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Michigan barrier free design: [R 408.30427](https://ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us/AdminCode/DownloadAdminCodeFile?FileName=R%20408.30401%20to%20R%20408.30499a.pdf) (section 1102.1: 1966 PA 1, the code and ICC A117.1 except sections 611 and 707), [MCL 125.1352](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-125-1352), [MCL 125.1355](https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-125-1355) and the [Barrier Free Design Board](https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/bcc/boards-commissions/barrier-free-design-board). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Michigan stall rules compared with the federal ones: [ICC A117.1-2017, sections 604.5, 604.9 and 604.10](https://up.codes/viewer/michigan/icc-a117.1-2017/chapter/6/plumbing-elements-and-facilities) and 2021 Michigan Building Code section 1110.2 (secondary copies) against the [2010 ADA Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/), sections 213.3.1, 604.5 and 604.8. Checked 2026-11-24.
